headline: Myanmar airstrikes resume after 7 months, triggering panic in Teknaf
summary: Powerful explosions from Maungdaw and Buthidaung townships were heard across the border, shaking houses and causing residents to flee their homes in fear.
details: Airstrikes in Myanmar’s Rakhine State near the Bangladesh border have reportedly resumed after nearly seven months, causing widespread panic among border residents.
Residents from Jadimura to Shah Porir Dwip in Teknaf reported hearing four powerful explosions shortly after 9:30 PM on Wednesday, which were strong enough to shake houses.
Teknaf Upazila Nirbahi Officer SM Anik Chowdhury confirmed that loud explosions were heard from inside Myanmar and that authorities are monitoring the situation.
The UNO stated that the airstrikes were carried out in the Maungdaw and Buthidaung townships of Myanmar.
Local resident Mohammad Salam described feeling a strong tremor that made it seem as though the ground was shaking, while seeing flames rising across the Naf river.
Sabrang Union Parishad member Abul Fayez noted that fighting has resumed in Myanmar after a prolonged lull, with the impact being felt strongly along the Teknaf border.
Many residents, particularly children and older people, rushed out of their homes in fear following the explosions.

The last major cross-border impact was reported on December 28 last year, when clashes between the Arakan Army and the Arakan Army and Myanmar’s military sent sounds of explosions and heavy gunfire across the border.

headline_marked: AI-generated fake admit cards: [[Two students punished]] for exam fraud
headline: AI-generated fake admit cards: Two students punished for exam fraud
summary: Two individuals attempted to enter an examination hall using admit cards created with Artificial Intelligence, leading to their immediate punishment.
details: Two students were punished after attempting to take an examination using fake admit cards generated by Artificial Intelligence.
The fraud was detected by officials during the verification process, preventing the unauthorized entry of the candidates.
The use of AI to forge official documents for academic fraud marks a new and concerning trend in examination malpractice.
Authorities have taken disciplinary action against the two individuals involved in the attempt.
